nodes.title: Bundles on the global curve
nodes.statement: For X/Fq smooth projective geometrically connected and a smooth affine model 𝒢/X with connected fibres and reductive generic fibre G, Bun_𝒢(S) is the groupoid of fppf-locally trivial 𝒢-torsors on X×S and equivariant isomorphisms. It is an Artin stack locally of finite type with affine diagonal. Its geometric stabilizers are affine finite-type group schemes; stabilizers of rational objects have finitely many Fq-points.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k=Fq, with function field F and characteristic p.

The generic group G/F is connected reductive. Its chosen model 𝒢/X is smooth affine with connected fibres and reductive over a nonempty open U. Split statements use the constant split reductive model unless stated otherwise.
Bundle statements apply over arbitrary k-schemes S; HN boundedness keeps central degree or its lattice quotient. Iwahori and shifted-HN statements use their specified GLn or PGL2 specialization.

sources.match: Notation 2.1(a) defines, for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve and a split reductive G, the stack Bun_G of G-bundles on X×S and its level variants Bun_{G,D}. Varshavsky does not prove algebraicity at this place; the algebraicity, local finite type and smoothness for the smooth connected-fibre model are the Heinloth result recalled in VL §12.1, cited as the second source.

§12.1 recalls Heinloth's Proposition 1: for a smooth affine group scheme over X with geometrically connected fibres, reductive over U and parahoric at the points of X∖U, the stack of torsors on X×S is a smooth algebraic stack, locally of finite type. This is the algebraicity part of the node.

proofSteps: Use effective fppf descent for torsors, including descent of arrows.
For GLn import algebraic vector bundles and construct bounded Quot atlases; for the smooth model use a faithful representation and reductions of structure group.
Represent the isomorphism sheaf by sections of the associated affine bundle. Apply properness of X and finite presentation to obtain the diagonal and stabilizer assertions.
acceptance: Keep the stack, its rational groupoid and its set of isomorphism classes distinct.
GLn torsors recover the imported rank-n vector bundles.

For a quasi-split reductive model this is the fixed-curve stack of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison §3.1 (CurveBundles, TauCetiRoadmap pull request #999). This node adds the parahoric connected-fibre models, the affine diagonal and the stabilizer statements, and agrees with §3.1 on the reductive case.

nodes.statement: At a 𝒢-bundle E, infinitesimal automorphisms, tangent classes and obstructions are H⁰(X,ad E), H¹(X,ad E), H²(X,ad E). The last vanishes on the curve, so Bun_𝒢 is smooth of local dimension −χ(X,ad E). For constant reductive G this is (g−1)dim G; a ramified model uses its actual adjoint-bundle Euler characteristic.

sources.match: Proposition 5.17(1) states that the Iwahori-level PGL₂ stack Bun_G(Σ) is smooth of pure dimension 3(g−1)+N, N being the number of geometric level points, and calls this standard. For Gm obtain dimension g−1 although Pic⁰ has dimension g.

nodes.title: Iwahori flags and fractional twists
nodes.statement: Bun_n(Σ) consists of rank-n bundles with, at each x∈Σ, a periodic chain E⊃E(−x/n)⊃⋯⊃E(−x), whose n successive quotients are line bundles on x×S. Extend the chain periodically to define fractional twists E(D) for D supported at the level with coefficients in (1/n)Z; for nonrational points use the chosen residue-field sections over S∞. Bun_PGLn(Σ) is the Picard-stack quotient. Fractional twisting induces Atkin–Lehner automorphisms.

Descend tensoring and fractional rotation through the Picard action, using residue-field base changes for infinity coefficients.

nodes.title: Slopes and Harder–Narasimhan data
nodes.statement: For a nonzero coherent sheaf F on X use class (rk F,deg F), slope deg/rk for positive rank and +∞ for torsion. The HN filtration has semistable quotients with strictly decreasing slopes. Its ordered quotient classes define an HN type; for G-bundles use canonical parabolic reductions and dominant rational coweight in the adjoint group. On classes χ((r,d),(r′,d′))=(1−g)rr′+rd′−r′d.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k=Fq, with function field F and characteristic p.

The generic group G/F is connected reductive. Its chosen model 𝒢/X is smooth affine with connected fibres and reductive over a nonempty open U. Split statements use the constant split reductive model unless stated otherwise.

sources.match: §2.1 defines the class (rank, degree) of a coherent sheaf on the curve, its slope with value ∞ in rank zero, the semistable subcategories of each slope, Harder–Narasimhan types with strictly decreasing slopes, and the Euler form ⟨(r,d),(r′,d′)⟩=(1−g)rr′+(rd′−r′d). Schiffmann treats coherent sheaves only; the G-bundle reductions in the node are not from this source.

proofSteps: Use Riemann–Roch and Serre duality on the imported coherent/vector-bundle theory for the Euler pairing.
Construct maximal destabilizing saturated subobjects, then induct on rank; uniqueness forces base-change compatibility.
For reductive G use canonical parabolic reductions; keep central degree separate from the adjoint instability coweight.
acceptance: The zero sheaf has an empty HN type; no slope is assigned to it.

nodes.title: Bounded bundle loci
nodes.statement: HN≤μ is an open substack of Bun_G. Fixing the relevant central degrees (or quotienting by a suitable central lattice) makes its bounded components of finite type. For a fixed coherent-sheaf class each HN type has finitely many rational isomorphism classes; requiring all slopes ≥0 gives finitely many such types and classes. An adjoint HN bound alone does not bound degrees of the centre.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k=Fq, with function field F and characteristic p.

The generic group G/F is connected reductive. Its chosen model 𝒢/X is smooth affine with connected fibres and reductive over a nonempty open U. Split statements use the constant split reductive model unless stated otherwise.
Bundle statements apply over arbitrary k-schemes S; HN boundedness keeps central degree or its lattice quotient. Iwahori and shifted-HN statements use their specified GLn or PGL2 specialization.

sources.locator: §2, Notation 2.1(b), p. 4; Lemma A.3, p. 29; §3, Lemma 3.1(a), p. 12
sources.match: Notation 2.1(b) defines Bun_G^{≤μ} by bounding deg B_λ by ⟨μ,λ⟩ over all B-structures and dominant λ of the adjoint torus, and states, by Lemma A.3, that it is open in Bun_G; Lemma 3.1(a) gives finite type and quasi-projectivity of the level versions of fixed component ν when the level is deep. The coherent-sheaf counting statements of the node are its own additions.

Lemma 12.1 (Behrend, Heinloth, Arasteh Rad–Hartl) embeds the model in SL(V) with quasi-affine quotient, so that Bun_G→Bun⁰_{GL_r} is representable, quasi-affine and of finite presentation; VL then defines finite-type truncations of Bun_G by pulling back the finite-type bounded opens of Bun⁰_{GL_r}, working with G_ad so that they are Ξ-invariant.

proofSteps: Embed the bounded bundle problem in bounded Quot families after twisting by a sufficiently positive divisor.
Use bounded cohomology and finite generation to obtain finite-type atlases; prove openness by specialization of HN polygons.
For coherent sheaves with slopes ≥0, ranks and nonnegative quotient degrees admit only finitely many decompositions of the fixed class.
acceptance: For Gm the HN condition in the adjoint group is vacuous but line-bundle degrees remain unbounded.
For GL2 of degree zero, HN≤μ excludes O(m)⊕O(−m) for sufficiently large m.

For GL_r vector bundles the open bounded loci and their finite type are AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #924), layer AL.3, 'Harder–Narasimhan polygon semicontinuity' and 'Bounded curve-bundle loci and shtuka truncations'.

nodes.title: Central lattices and finite quotients
nodes.statement: Choose a discrete subgroup Ξ of Z(F)\Z(A) whose image controls the free central-degree directions and is cocompact in the required central quotient, with the usual injectivity condition preventing extra stabilizers. Central tensoring acts on bundles and shtukas. Bounded shtuka loci modulo Ξ have finitely many remaining degree components; rational stabilizer weights are retained. For GLn, a nonzero-degree idele a gives the quotient by a^Z.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k=Fq, with function field F and characteristic p.

The generic group G/F is connected reductive. Its chosen model 𝒢/X is smooth affine with connected fibres and reductive over a nonempty open U. Split statements use the constant split reductive model unless stated otherwise.
Bundle statements apply over arbitrary k-schemes S; HN boundedness keeps central degree or its lattice quotient. Iwahori and shifted-HN statements use their specified GLn or PGL2 specialization.

sources.match: On p. 59 VL lets Z(F)\Z(A) act on the shtuka stacks through Bun_Z,N(F_q), notes that the action preserves the Harder–Narasimhan truncations (taken on the adjoint torsor) and commutes with partial Frobenius, fixes a lattice Ξ in Z(F)\Z(A), and states that the truncations modulo Ξ are Deligne–Mumford of finite type. Remark 8.21 uses the same Ξ in the adelic quotient. The GLn example with a nonzero-degree idele is an illustration added here.

proofSteps: Use the idele-degree exact sequence to isolate the free central directions.
Check the tensor action and level compatibility, then choose Ξ so the remaining central degrees form a finite set.

nodes.title: Weil descent on full cohomology

The proof of 8.2.4 contains the slip recorded as finding E6.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.3.4 and Lemma 1.3.11, pp. 11–12; §6, Lemma 6.0.9 and Proposition 6.0.10, p. 35

proofSteps: For a finite module M over a finitely generated commutative O_E-algebra A, reduce modulo powers of every maximal ideal. If λ lies in the maximal ideal the quotients are finite torsion O_E-modules; otherwise they are finite-dimensional E-modules. Apply the corresponding finite-coefficient or rational Drinfeld lemma; do not use the incorrect assertion that every quotient is torsion over O_E.
Use Krull intersection and localization to kill the Frobenius–Weil kernel on M. In the split integral case use finiteness over one local Hecke algebra.

For nonsplit rational coefficients use finite Hecke envelopes supplied by the Eichler–Shimura recurrence and finite local Hecke tensor products; take their directed union. This uses semisimplicity of the rational representation category, not an integral semisimplicity claim.
acceptance: A finite A-module is not necessarily finite over O_E.

review.reason: Xue's proof of Lemma 8.2.4 (arXiv v2, p. 55) asserts that A/m^n is a finite torsion O_E-module for every maximal ideal m of a finitely generated O_E-algebra A. For A=O_E[t], m=(λt−1) is maximal with A/m=E, which is neither finite nor torsion over O_E. The two-case repair is correct. If λ∈m, A/m is a finite field (a finitely generated algebra over the residue field), so M/m^nM is a finite torsion O_E-module and Lemma 8.2.2 applies. If λ∉m, λ is invertible in A/m^n, A/m is a finite extension of E by Zariski's lemma, and M/m^nM is a finite-dimensional E-space. By the continuity convention of 8.2.3 it contains a lattice stable under π_1^geom, so the E-coefficient Drinfeld lemma (Xue's earlier Lemma 3.2.13, VL Lemme 8.2 after inverting λ) applies. Krull intersection and localization then finish as printed. The proposition is unaffected.
